reading the first character of the formatted buffer

states.claim: tmpbuf points to the mutable data buffer of tmpstr, a String with reserved capacity 63.

L21: String tmpstr(63, ReserveString);

states.claim: tmpbuf is reassigned to point to the mutable data buffer of tmpstr after tmpstr is reallocated with capacity tmplen.
states.evidence:
L31: tmpstr = String(tmplen, ReserveString);
L32: tmpbuf = tmpstr.mutableData();

states.claim: dp points to the first decimal point character within tmpbuf, or is NULL if dec is zero or no decimal point is found.
states.evidence:
L43: dp = strpbrk(tmpbuf, ".,");
L45: dp = nullptr;

states.claim: resbuf points to the mutable data buffer of resstr, a String with reserved capacity reslen.
states.evidence:
L84: String resstr(reslen, ReserveString);
L85: resbuf = resstr.mutableData();

states.claim: s points to the last character of the formatted number in tmpbuf.
t points to the last byte of the reserved buffer of resstr.
resstr is resized to reslen before being returned.

values.claim: tmpstr is reserved with capacity 63; tmpbuf points to its mutable data; snprintf is called with buffer size 64, so the first snprintf may write up to 64 bytes including the NUL terminator.
If the first snprintf returns tmplen >= 64, tmpstr is reallocated with capacity tmplen and tmpbuf is updated to the new mutable data; the second snprintf is called with buffer size tmplen + 1.
If dec is nonzero, dp is the first '.' or ',' in tmpbuf; otherwise dp is null. If dp is non-null, integral = dp - tmpbuf; otherwise integral = tmplen.
When thousand_sep is non-empty, integral is increased by ((integral-1)/3) * thousand_sep.size(), after an overflow check.
reslen starts as integral; if dec is nonzero, reslen is increased by dec and, if dec_point is non-empty, by dec_point.size().
If is_negative is true, reslen is incremented by 1 for the minus sign.
resstr is allocated with size reslen and resbuf points to its mutable data.
values.evidence:
L84: String resstr(reslen, ReserveString);
L85: resbuf = resstr.mutableData();

values.claim: s is initialized to tmpbuf + tmplen - 1, pointing at the last character of the formatted number.
t is initialized to resbuf + reslen - 1, pointing at the last byte of the result buffer.
If dec is nonzero, declen is the number of characters after the decimal point: s - dp if dp is non-null, otherwise 0.

L94: int declen = dp ? s - dp : 0;

values.claim: If dp is non-null, t is decreased by declen.
If dp is non-null, declen bytes starting at dp+1 are copied to t+1.
If dec_point is non-empty, dec_point.size() bytes from dec_point.data() are copied to t + (1 - dec_point.size()), and t is decreased by dec_point.size().
values.evidence:
L112: memcpy(t + (1 - dec_point.size()), dec_point.data(), dec_point.size());
L113: t -= dec_point.size();

values.claim: The loop copies characters from s down to tmpbuf into t, decrementing both; every third copied character, if thousand_sep is non-empty and s is still >= tmpbuf, thousand_sep is copied to t + (1 - thousand_sep.size()) and t is decreased by thousand_sep.size().
If is_negative is true, a '-' is stored at t and t is decremented.
resstr is set to size reslen before being returned.
